title: Aaron Boone: Jazz Chisholm Jr. ‘not a dumb guy’ after postgame confusion in Tampa
content:
ST PETERSBURG, Fla. — A day after Jazz Chisholm Jr. admitted he was unaware of MLB’s forceout rule following a costly bobble in the 10th inning Saturday, his manager backed the New York Yankees’ second baseman, insisting there was no doubt he understood exactly what the situation demanded.

“He’s not confused,” Aaron Boone said. “I think that’s his kind of default answer when he’s got (reporters) in front of him.”

With the score tied at 4-4 and one out in Saturday’s game, Tampa Bay Rays first baseman Jonathan Aranda chopped a grounder to Chisholm. Tampa had the bases loaded, so the only way for New York to extend the game if there was a batted ball was to either throw the runner out at home plate or turn a double play. But with how softly Aranda’s batted ball was, Chisholm had to turn a double play because throwing home to get Chandler Simpson out at the plate was impossible. But none of it mattered because Chisholm bobbled the ball, and the Rays won.

After Saturday’s game, Boone said he was unsure if Chisholm could have turned the double play if he had fielded the ball cleanly. Yandy Díaz was running from first base and slowed down on the basepath while running to second. Chisholm would have had to tag Díaz, or hope for an out-of-the-baseline call, and throw the ball to first base to beat Aranda.

“It turns out to be a tough play,” Boone said Sunday. “Watching it back, there might have been a chance if he gets it cleanly, he gets the tag off. It’s hard to know how exactly Díaz reacts in that moment. Once it chops like that, you know it’s obviously going to be a tough one to turn the normal 4-6-3.”

The social media response to Chisholm saying he didn’t know a common baseball rule has been intense. Boone said he believes Chisholm should have answered the questions after Saturday’s game in a “better way,” but he defended the infielder from attacks on his baseball IQ.

“He’s not a dumb guy,” Boone said. “It’s just sometimes how you present yourself in certain situations, and coupled with he’s off to a little bit of a slow start.”

This is the most important season for Chisholm. He will be a free agent at the end of the year, and he’s been vocal with his goals of wanting to join the 50-50 club with Shohei Ohtani. But Chisholm has struggled at the plate. Entering Sunday’s game, Chisholm had a .482 OPS with no home runs and six stolen bases. Chisholm said Saturday that he feels like most of his at-bats have ended in popups. He also said earlier in the week that most of his struggles were related to the cold weather and the inability to feel the bat in his hands.

“Jazz is gonna hit,” Boone said. “Jazz will get it going. It’s just working on getting that ball on a line.”
